D-006/COUNCIL: dev-trv-1110 rejected D1-016/D1-017 because their cannot-compile-READY gates pass under needs-consent without ever testing freshness or realization. Strengthened, never weakened: forced authority=allowed one-factor Worlds, explicit state/blocker assertions, one positive control per task, original assertions kept.

D-20261007-14329: the D1-017 gate 'an explicit unknown target never resolves to another Account' only exercised the quoted form, so its name overstated what it proved (unquoted 'send hello to Gemini' still retargeted to claude-work). Strengthened, not renamed: the same assertions now run over both quoted and unquoted forms.

D-20261007-14329 follow-up: dev-trv-d14329 rejected D1-017 because the gate proved two exact strings while six variants still retargeted to claude-work (trailing ! ? -, a quote after the route). Gate now iterates the class: terminators, trailing clause, quote after route, unknown multi-word target. Stricter only; name unchanged.

D-20261008-013: new separate gate 'an unheld recipient named beside a held one is never dropped' for the residual R2 (send hello to Gemini via work claude was READY on claude-work). Added gate only; no existing gate widened or renamed.

D-20261008-015: new separate gate 'an unheld recipient sharing a preposition with a held one is never dropped' for the preposition-ellipsis residual (send hello to Gemini and work claude was READY on claude-work). Added gate only; nothing widened or renamed.

D-20261008-016: three new separate gates: (1) 'a recipient that only partly matches a Provider is not held' (personal claude READY on claude-work), (2) 'an unheld recipient joined by punctuation is never dropped' (work claude, Gemini READY), (3) 'a clause after a held recipient is not a second recipient' (pins the fail-safe over-refusal of 'and say thanks' to READY, both ways). Added gates only; nothing widened or renamed.

D1-006.head: f9f82a146fb0
D1-006.note: Code change confined to validate.ts (a-truth.gate.test.ts untouched; only generated projections alongside). Gate at test/gates/a-truth.gate.test.ts:75 now discriminates: pre-fix 'send x to mailbox home' on W4 (worlds/W4.json: authority prompt.send@1=consent-required, sole realization d1-virtual.prompt.send@1 serves provider:claude only) returned needs-consent, which is outside the allowed set, so the gate was red; validate.ts:121-129 adds the provider-serving check returning unavailable. Evidence file shows exactly one flip (fail->pass) and pass 39->40 with REGRESSED 0. No side effects: the loop only reads, mirrors the existing decl.params.find(...)! pattern at validate.ts:79, and the !account continue is unreachable-as-a-hole because heldBy already routed unknown ids to needs-info. Compatible targets unaffected (verified: W4 claude-work -> needs-consent / ready / refused under consent-required/allowed/denied). Ordering: the new check sits after the pre-existing capability-level realization check and before authority, so incompatible -> unavailable under all three authority states; this is the established convention, not a new inversion, but it means denied+incompatible now reports unavailable rather than refused -- an inherited-ordering observation for the ordering owner. Two scope notes, neither a defect in this commit: (1) this commit added no tests -- 2 of the 3 promoted D1-006 gates were already green from bc226dc, so D1-006 must not be read later as 'three new tests written'; the locked gate is also a permissive negative (allows unavailable/needs-choice/unknown/refused) rather than asserting unavailable plus its reason. (2) The fix is provider-only and ignores freshness, while the module's canonical compatibleAccounts (src/world.ts:92-95) also requires freshness==='fresh': on W3 the stale account yields compatibleAccounts=[] yet validateInterpretation returns needs-consent, and ready under authority=allowed. That is pre-existing, not introduced here, and belongs to D1-016/D1-017, not to D1-006's closure.

D1-016.head: 2a81cf06fec2
D1-016.note: Gate 'W3 stale Account can never yield a READY command' (b-world.gate.test.ts:57) is non-discriminating: probe shows W3-as-authored and W3-mutated-to-freshness=fresh give IDENTICAL validation (needs-consent, account=account:claude-work, unresolved=[]). With authority.prompt.send@1=allowed the STALE account compiles state=READY, unresolved=[]. compile.ts:571-580 records no blocker for an explicitly named Account the World holds, so freshness never reaches the compiled command. Gate 1 (compatibleAccounts==[]) is genuine; gate 2 is green only because every D1 world sets prompt.send@1=consent-required.

D1-016.head: ee1be8a11d71
D1-016.note: ACCEPT (independent, adversarial). Verified at HEAD 76fe02b, working tree clean for the reviewed files. Gate hardening is real: both original D1-016 assertions are retained verbatim and four gates now run under a forced authority=allowed World (b-world.gate.test.ts:72-86), so the verdict is decided by freshness rather than by needs-consent. Discrimination proven by mutation, not by reading: deleting the single freshness line (validate.ts:130) from a /tmp copy turns EXACTLY one gate red - 'W3 stale Account is refused for freshness even when authority allows it' - while the pre-existing 'W3 stale Account can never yield a READY command' stays green, which is the direct confirmation of dev-trv-1110's finding that the original gate was vacuous. Positive control is one-factor: with the authority map merged identically in both arms, W3-stale -> needs-info ('account: \account:claude-work\ is stale, not fresh') and W3-fresh -> ready. The blocker is load-bearing end to end, not just a label: dispatch commit is rejected NOT_READY needs-info for the stale Account and granted only for the fresh control; granting consent does not revive it. Freshness is read in exactly one readiness place (validate.ts:130) and precedes realization and authority (validate.ts:131-137); observable proof of the ordering is that W3 at its authored consent-required authority now returns needs-info/stale rather than needs-consent. No bypass exists: commit is gated by validation() (session.ts:67-68) and project.ts:101 reports ready only from an accepted commit; executeVirtual is still a stub. RESIDUAL GAPS (recorded, not blocking): (1) no gate pins the freshness-before-authority ORDERING - a one-line assertion that fixture W3 (consent-required) returns needs-info with a /stale/ reason would lock COUNCIL's requirement down; (2) the gate would also pass if freshness were implemented as a compile-path blocker in unresolvedFor, so it pins behaviour but not the architectural placement inside the one READY law; (3) spec.json still declares D1-016 surface as src/world.ts + worlds/, while the implementation now lives in validate.ts (D1-005's file) - a provenance/surface mismatch worth reconciling. Freshness verdict state 'needs-info' is a reasonable, internally consistent label here: contract.ts:121 has no 'stale' verdict, and the compile path already mapped its 'stale' unresolved reason to needs-info, so the two paths agree.

D1-017.head: 2a81cf06fec2
D1-017.note: Gate 'W4 unknown and incompatible targets cannot compile READY' (b-world.gate.test.ts:67) is non-discriminating: 'send x to mailbox home' gives IDENTICAL validation (needs-consent, account=account:mailbox-home, unresolved=[]) whether or not provider:mailbox has a prompt.send realization. With authority=allowed, the mailbox Account (no realization) compiles state=READY, and 'send x to Gemini' SILENTLY RETARGETS to account=account:claude-work and compiles READY via the single-compatible fallback at compile.ts:508-511 - the exact D1-005/U1 defect. Gate 1 (compatibleAccounts==[WORK]) is genuine; gate 2 is green only because every D1 world sets prompt.send@1=consent-required.

D1-017.head: ee1be8a11d71
D1-017.note: ACCEPT (independent, adversarial) with one named residual hole. Verified at HEAD 76fe02b, working tree clean for the reviewed files. All three original D1-017 assertions are retained and three gates were added under forced authority=allowed (b-world.gate.test.ts:101-125). Discrimination proven by mutation on a /tmp copy, each mutation turning EXACTLY one gate red: reverting the draftFor mention guard (compile.ts:528) -> 'an explicit unknown target never resolves to another Account' fails; removing the unresolvedFor unknown branch (compile.ts:607) -> same gate fails on reason/options; removing the unheldRoute wiring (compile.ts:155) -> same gate fails because the mention never appears; removing the per-Account realization check (validate.ts:131-132) -> 'an Account no realization serves is unavailable even when authority allows it' fails. Every half of the fix is independently load-bearing. Defect reproduction matches dev-trv-1110 exactly: at d20d605 (hardened gates, pre-fix code) 'send x to Gemini' under W4 with authority=allowed resolved to account:claude-work, validated ready and COMMITTED; at HEAD it resolves to account=null with unresolved=[account:unknown, options:[]] and commit is rejected NOT_READY. The old single-compatible fallback is therefore discriminated against, and unresolvedFor no longer offers the compatible set as the choice on offer (pre-fix it offered both accounts). No regression anywhere: full-suite probe diff d20d605 -> HEAD is exactly two gates newly green (the two new D-016/D-017 gates) and zero newly red across all 85 gates; ratchet status --probe reports REGRESSED 0. RESIDUAL GAPS (recorded, follow-up warranted, not a rejection): (1) the retarget hole is closed only for QUOTED payloads, exactly as compile.ts:487-491 documents. 'send hello to Gemini' (unquoted) under W1/W4 with authority=allowed STILL resolves to account:claude-work and compiles READY and commits - the same U1 defect class. The promoted gate name 'an explicit unknown target never resolves to another Account' is therefore broader than the behaviour it exercises; recommend either renaming it to state the quoted-payload scope, or opening an explicit gate for the unquoted case so the boundary is a measured claim rather than a comment. (2) unheldRoute over-captures post-quote clauses that are not routes: 'send x about the outage', 'send x for review', 'send x into the fire' now refuse as unknown targets where they previously defaulted; this fails safe (never retargets) and regresses no promoted gate, but it is an untested narrowing of the phrase surface. (3) unheldRoute cannot capture payload words or steal a grounded target - it only fires when grounding found nothing and only when a quote exists, so payloadOf always returns the quote verbatim; verified across 'with urgency to work claude', 'via/from/at work claude', 'to work claude please', all still READY. (4) allowedAuthority()'s unused patch parameter is dead code in a hardened gate file. (5) unrelated pre-existing behaviour, not introduced here: W2 'send x' with no route reports needs-info/missing rather than needs-choice, identically before and after this change (compile.ts:274 maps every non-ambiguous blocker to needs-info).

D1-017.head: 21ee385bd7fa
D1-017.note: REJECT. Gate strengthening is real and non-vacuous (46de059: name unchanged, quoted assertions kept, loop over both forms; mutant 1 revert-of-cc2e96f and mutant 2 'unheldRoute returns null when no quote' both turn it red). But the property the gate NAMES is still false on shipped code: an unrecognised explicit target on the unquoted path still fills the single compatible Account and reaches ready. Seven natural utterances with authority allowed on W4 return account=account:claude-work, state=ready, no unresolved record: 'send hello to Gemini!', 'send hello to Gemini?', 'send hello to the team!', 'send hello to Gemini - thanks', "send hello to Gemini 'x'", 'send hello to Gemini "x"'. Root cause 1 compile.ts:508 'if (tail.some(t => t.kind !== "word" && t.kind !== "punct")) return null;' - '!', '?' and '-' lex as kind 'symbol' (only ',' and '.' are 'punct'), so any sentence-final symbol silently disarms the unheld-route guard and falls through to the single-compatible fill. Root cause 2 compile.ts:499-500 'const q = body.findIndex(quote); const from = q < 0 ? 0 : q + 1;' - a quote token anywhere after the route makes 'from' skip past the preposition, the loop never runs, and the route is dropped. Fairness: not a regression - at bd241e2 ten of twelve probe forms retargeted; cc2e96f narrows the class to these six but does not close it. The gate cannot see the residue because it tests exactly 'send hello to Gemini' with no terminator and no trailing token, and mutant 3 (dropping 'on' from TARGET_PREPS) stays green, so the gate is also silent on the fail-safe false-positive side ('send hello on Monday' becomes unknown-target needs-info). Governance: b-world.gate.test.ts is anchored, so state.ts:105 consults only the spec-change digest and state.ts:120 lists only non-promoted gates in 'promotable' - the strengthened gate keeps promoted provenance specDigest sha256:4444b120 / by dev-impl-d006 / head f6c603d69bcd while the file is now sha256:b0b2b172, so check emits no SPEC_CHANGED and no PROMOTE_PENDING and verify prints [promoted] by dev-impl-d006. dev-d006 re-promoted after its own spec-change; dev-d14329 did not. verify D1-017 green, status --probe REGRESSED 0, check exit 0 (5 pre-existing warnings).

D1-017.head: fa0401427d32
D1-017.note: ACCEPT (independent, adversarial, mutation-tested; label dev-trv-d14329b). Prior reject dev-trv-d14329 is answered on every disarm it named. Scope: 2aabfed (gate), f0f30a0 (fix), 3917d73 (projections). HEAD advanced 3917d73 -> fa04014 mid-review; the two intervening commits touch neither experimental/d1 nor experimental/ratchet, so D1-017 code+spec are byte-identical to 3917d73. GATE (upheld): name 'an explicit unknown target never resolves to another Account, even with authority allowed' is byte-identical across 2aabfed^/2aabfed/HEAD; all five D1-017 gates retained, none renamed or removed (b-world.gate.test.ts:88,93,101,121,129). 2aabfed is +6/-2, strictly stricter: only the loop's string list grew, every assertion at :110-117 is retained. SPEC_CHANGE is real: 2aabfed recorded it in ratchet.lock.json and the on-disk file digest sha256:ebc1758... matches the recorded 'to' exactly, so check correctly emits no SPEC_CHANGED -- the prior reviewer's governance gap is closed. CODE (upheld): f0f30a0 is confined to omega-baseline/experimental/d1/src/compile.ts and, inside it, to unheldRoute (compile.ts:500-510); 3917d73 regenerates only .project/evidence/d1-ratchet.json and .project/ratchet/D1-BOARD.md. VERIFY: RATCHET_MODE=probe bun run ratchet verify D1-017 -> 'D1-017 PROVEN', all 5 gates [promoted], exit 0. STATUS: bun run ratchet status --probe -> probe 0137952be72a (45/85 green); DONE 14 / PROVEN 15 / OPEN 11 / BLOCKED 37 / REGRESSED 0. CHECK: exit 0, 'check ok (5 warning(s))', all five PROMOTE_PENDING are unrelated to D1-017. NO REGRESSION: full-suite gate outcome set (pass/fail per gate, 125 lines) is byte-identical between 46de059 and HEAD -- zero newly-red, zero newly-green. MUTATION (each on a disposable /tmp worktree, all removed): (a) compile.ts reverted to f0f30a0^ -> gate FAILS at b-world.gate.test.ts:110 (Expected: not 'ready'). (b) unheldRoute made to REQUIRE a quote token -> gate FAILS, same line: the unquoted form retargets. (c) unheldRoute disabled (return null) -> gate FAILS, same line. So all three prior disarmings -- trailing ! ? -, trailing clause, quote after route -- are each independently load-bearing and discriminated against by a red gate. PROBES (authority forced allowed via fixture spread + prompt.send@1=allowed; W4 unless noted; account never filled): every one of the 7 gate strings returns state=needs-info, account=null, provider=null, unresolved=[account=unknown, options=[]], reason 'account: "gemini" grounded to no account' ('the team' for the multi-word case) -- needs-info, never ready, never claude-work. Also: 'send hello to Gemini.' needs-info/no fill; 'send hello to Gemini, please' needs-info/no fill; 'send hello to Gemini "x"' needs-info/no fill; 'send hello to work claude!' ready/account:claude-work (correct, held route); 'send hello to work claude' ready/account:claude-work; W1 'send hello' ready/account:claude-work (unchanged default fill); W2 'send hello to claude!' needs-choice, provider:provider:claude, options=[account:claude-personal, account:claude-work] (ambiguity preserved, D1 never picks); 'send \'tell it to Gemini\' to work claude' ready/account:claude-work with prompt exactly 'tell it to Gemini' -- quoted payload untouched and never retargets; 'send \'x\' about the outage' ready/account:claude-work with prompt 'x' -- 'about' correctly not a target preposition. ZERO false negatives among the gate strings and their near neighbours. RESIDUALS (recorded, follow-up warranted, NOT grounds for rejection -- each is byte-identical at bd241e2, 46de059 and HEAD, i.e. neither introduced nor closed by f0f30a0): (R1) params.prompt still carries the route words when a non-word token follows the route: 'send hello to Gemini!' -> prompt 'hello to Gemini!' (not 'hello'). Root cause compile.ts:525 -- payloadOf returns a CONTIGUOUS text.slice from the first unconsumed token to the last, so an unconsumed trailing '!' extends the slice back over the consumed route. It also hits HELD routes: 'send hello to work claude!' is READY with prompt 'hello to work claude!'. Confirmed pre-existing and unchanged by this fix. (R2) multi-recipient utterances still fill: 'send hello to Gemini via work claude', 'send hello to work claude and to Gemini', 'send hello to Gemini, then to work claude' all return ready/account:claude-work with the unheld target silently dropped. Root cause compile.ts:155 -- unheldRoute runs only when grounded.mention === null, so once the grounder finds the held 'work claude' the unheld mention is never read. Identical at bd241e2 and 46de059. The gate NAME still claims 'never', which is broader than the single-recipient behaviour exercised; per 'no rename hiding gaps' the right follow-up is an explicit gate for the multi-recipient class, not a rename. (R3) fail-safe false positive, documented in the code comment at compile.ts:489-499 and unchanged by f0f30a0: 'on' is a TARGET_PREP, so 'send hello on Monday' refuses as unknown target needs-info/monday, and 'send hello to Gemini on Friday' refuses on 'friday'. Fails safe, never retargets, but it narrows the phrase surface with no gate pinning it. (R4) COVERAGE GAP, new evidence: the gate is insensitive to mention CONTENT. Mutant (b') unheldRoute's word-run extended to the end of the utterance (terminators and all) stays GREEN. It degrades the mention to 'gemini !', 'gemini ?', 'gemini - thanks', 'gemini x', 'the team !' while the no-fill property still holds, so the directive is not violated -- but the gate asserts reason/options/account only (b-world.gate.test.ts:110-117) and never the mention string, so any future regression that keeps the decision and corrupts the mention would pass silently. A single expect on the mention text for 'the team' would close it. (R5) HEAD moved during review and the working tree carries pre-existing uncommitted .project/ edits from concurrent council/devops sessions; neither affects the D1-017 code or spec digest.

D1-017.head: 7a96038951c2
D1-017.note: ACCEPT (adversarial, mutation-tested; no --reject). SCOPE: bc39ae1 adds one gate() block, +21/-0 lines, 0 deletions (own gate, nothing widened); machine diff of every gate id+name in the whole gates dir vs bc39ae1~1 shows exactly one ADDITION and zero renames/removals. 79c204d touches compile.ts only (+46/-1). RED-BEFORE-FIX confirmed. MUTATION (disposable worktree, all three fire): (a) revert compile.ts to bc39ae1 -> D1-017 FAILS at 'Expected: not ready'; (b) unheldLink forced to return null -> FAILS; (c) add 'on' to CHAIN_PREPS -> control 'send note on Monday to work claude' FAILS (got needs-info, expected ready). ratchet verify D1-017 green; status --probe REGRESSED 0, 46/86 (45/85 -> 46/86, +1 gate +1 pass, nothing else moved); ratchet check exit 0, 5 pre-existing PROMOTE_PENDING warnings on unrelated tasks. PROBES (W4, authority prompt.send@1=allowed unless noted): 'send hello to Gemini via work claude', "send 'x' to Gemini via work claude", 'send hello to work claude and to Gemini', 'send hello to Gemini, then to work claude', 'send hello to work claude via Gemini', 'send hello to Gemini or to work claude' -> all needs-info, account=null, unresolved account:unknown (Gemini no longer absorbed). No false positives introduced; fail-safe only tightens. Bonus: fix also stops Gemini leaking into the prompt body (pre-fix prompt was 'hello to Gemini').
